programs.haiku:
"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj component 4416, as a readable program.

What it does, in plain terms:
  * It is quiet (near 0) on most text, with a small diffuse wobble that this program does not model.
  * It goes clearly negative on a score unit right after a number: "2 points", "1 point",
    "10 pts", "3 marks", "4 stars", "5 ratings". The strongest cases are points and marks
    on exams and quizzes.
  * It is also negative on the academic sense of "credit" ("extra credit", "earn credit",
    "give credit to"), and more weakly on other units after a number ("3 ms", "5 分", "(16%)").
  * On the first token of a document, where the model sees no earlier context, it sits
    slightly positive, about +0.1 on average.

Everything is read from the last one or two tokens, so no carried state is needed.
A document starts where the document id changes, as in the model's own attention resets.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Score or award units that dip hard when they follow a number.
SCORE_UNITS = {"point", "points", "pts", "pt", "marks", "mark"}
# Rating units that dip when they follow a number.
RATING_UNITS = {"stars", "star", "ratings", "rating"}
# Units that dip only a little when they follow a number.
MILD_UNITS = {"ms", "分", "%)"}
# Words that, just before "credit", mark the academic or award sense.
CREDIT_CUES = {"earn", "extra", "give", "gives", "given", "giving", "get", "myself",
               "appropriate", "college", "bonus", "full", "partial", "valid"}

HAS_DIGIT = re.compile(r"\d")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return carry, 0.1  # first token of a document: a small positive offset
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower()
    after_number = bool(HAS_DIGIT.search(prev))
    if after_number:
        if word in SCORE_UNITS:
            return carry, -2.5
        if word in RATING_UNITS:
            return carry, -0.8
        if word in MILD_UNITS:
            return carry, -0.4
    if word == "credit" and prev in CREDIT_CUES:
        return carry, -2.5
    return carry, 0.0

"""Web-page metadata lines. The activation fires on the line break that closes a short,
non-prose metadata line: a timestamp, a byline, or a counter such as views, posts,
replies, answers, kudos, or a forum/profile label. Fires harder when a clock time or a
date is on the line. Negative on the space typed right after 'Month day,' (a year follows).
Also fires on the line break after a chat-template 'user' header."""
import re

READS = ()

MONTH = r"\b(?:Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Sept|Oct|Nov|Dec)[a-z]*\.?"
DATE = re.compile(MONTH + r"|\b(?:19|20)\d\d\b")
TIME = re.compile(r"\d{1,2}:\d\d")
META = re.compile(
    r"(?i)\b(views?|posts?|posted|joined|kudos|repl(?:y|ies)|answers?|comments?|permalink|"
    r"edited|published|updated|last|date|category|tags?|author|share|by|ago|today|yesterday|"
    r"followers?|likes?|ratings?|pages?|user|utc|am|pm|monday|tuesday|wednesday|thursday|"
    r"friday|saturday|sunday)\b|阅读|浏览|件"
)
PROSE = re.compile(r"[a-z]{2,} [a-z]{2,} [a-z]{2,}")
DAY_COMMA = re.compile(MONTH + r"\s+\d{1,2}(?:st|nd|rd|th)?,\s$")


def line_value(text):
    text = text.strip()
    if len(text) > 40 or PROSE.search(text):
        return 0.0
    value = 0.0
    if META.search(text):
        value += 1.0
    if DATE.search(text):
        value += 0.6
    if TIME.search(text):
        value += 1.0
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    line, doc = carry if carry is not None else ("", None)
    t = prefix.position
    s = prefix.token_strings[t]
    if prefix.document_ids[t] != doc:
        line = ""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[t]
    value = 0.0
    if "\n" in s:
        if line.endswith("<|im_start|>user"):
            value = 1.0
        else:
            value = line_value(line)
        line = ""
    else:
        if DAY_COMMA.search(line + s):
            value = -1.1
        line = line + s
    return (line, doc), value

"""Approximate short determiner constructions, rather than general word meaning.

After a/an, specificity and ranking phrases usually contribute negatively;
degree modifiers and collection phrases contribute positively. Quantifiers
change the strength, and some selection words reverse sign after the.
Also recognize a few relative-clause frames and the Latin phrase per se.
All other tokens are predicted as zero; document boundaries clear the history.
"""
READS = ()

SPECIFIC = {'specific', 'specified', 'particular', 'individual', 'certain'}
ORDINARY = {'regular', 'typical', 'standard', 'normal', 'average', 'general'}
PRAISE = {'good', 'great', 'excellent', 'perfect', 'fine', 'beautiful'}
DEGREE = {'very', 'extremely', 'really', 'pretty', 'quite', 'rather',
          'seriously', 'incredibly'}
INTEREST = {'interesting', 'exciting', 'fascinating', 'intriguing'}
COLLECTION = {'combination', 'mixture', 'mix', 'variety', 'bunch'}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        prev = before = ''
    else:
        _, prev, before = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    w, p = token.strip().lower(), prev.strip().lower()
    value = 0.0
    # Do not mistake the final 'a' of a split word for an article.
    boundary = (prev.startswith(' ') or not before or
                before[-1:].isspace() or before == '<|endoftext|>')
    article = p in {'a', 'an'} and boundary
    if article and token.startswith(' '):
        if w == 'given': value = -3.35
        elif w in SPECIFIC: value = -0.85
        elif w in {'complete', 'comprehensive', 'absolute'}: value = -1.2
        elif w in {'whole', 'entire', 'full'}: value = -0.35
        elif w in ORDINARY: value = -0.85 if w != 'general' else -0.3
        elif w in PRAISE: value = -0.65 if w != 'great' else -0.2
        elif w in DEGREE: value = 1.05 if w != 'pretty' else 1.85
        elif w in INTEREST: value = 1.55
        elif w in COLLECTION:
            value = (2.3 if w == 'combination' else
                     1.5 if w == 'variety' else 1.0)
        elif w == 'different': value = 1.35
        elif w == 'part': value = -1.9
        elif w == 'person': value = -0.9
        elif w == 'first': value = -1.4
        elif w == 'fastest': value = -1.9
        elif w == 'set': value = -0.7
        elif w == 'one': value = -0.65
        elif w == 'matter': value = -0.5
        elif w == 'considerable': value = -1.4
        elif w in {'nice', 'helpful', 'chance', 'free', 'quick', 'fun'}: value = 0.8
        elif w in {'necessary', 'exact', 'proper'}: value = -1.3
        elif w == 'long': value = -0.45
        elif w in {'estimated', 'expected', 'unexpected', 'actual'}:
            value = 1.1
    elif p in {'any', 'no', 'every', 'each', 'some'} and token.startswith(' '):
        if w in {'one', 'body'}:
            if p == 'any': value = -4.2
            elif p == 'every': value = -3.2
            elif p == 'some': value = -2.5
            else: value = -1.3
        elif w == 'given': value = -6.0
        elif w in SPECIFIC: value = -2.3 if p == 'any' else -1.3
        elif w == 'other' and p != 'each': value = -0.9
        elif p == 'some' and w in DEGREE: value = 3.0
    elif p == 'the':
        if w in {'given', 'specified', 'correct', 'necessary', 'desired',
                 'indicated', 'free', 'wrong', 'usual', 'attached'}:
            value = 0.6
        elif w == 'one': value = -0.9
    if w == 'of' and before.strip().lower() in {'a', 'an'}:
        if p == 'combination': value = 1.8
        elif p == 'part': value = -1.1
    if w == 'se' and p == 'per': value = -2.8
    elif w == 'que':
        if p == 'con': value = -0.95
        elif p in {'la', 'las'}: value = 0.65
    return (doc, token, prev), value
programs.haiku:
"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj component 4418, explained as a word-class detector.

The component is quiet on most tokens. Its large values come on the word right after an
indefinite determiner ("a", "an", "any", "some", "no", "every"), and the sign depends on
which word that is:

- "given" after a determiner is strongly negative: "a given set", "any given".
- Specifying words are moderately negative: "a particular", "a specific", "a certain",
  "a complete", "a first", "a part of", "any one", "the one", "a good".
- Degree adverbs and mixture/variety nouns are moderately positive: "a very", "a pretty",
  "a different", "a variety of", "a combination of", "a mix of", "a bunch of".

Three smaller patterns sit outside that frame:

- "Title:" (the colon right after "Title") is strongly positive.
- Chinese and Japanese copula/focus words ("的是", "のは", "都是", "是一", ...) are
  moderately positive.

Everything else predicts zero. The program reads only the previous and current token, and
it resets at a document boundary.
"""

READS = ()

DETERMINERS = {" a", " an", " any", " some", " no", " every"}

# "one" is negative after "the" and "each" too ("the one", "each one").
ONE_CONTEXTS = DETERMINERS | {" the", " each"}

GIVEN_VALUE = -3.5

SPECIFIERS = {
    " particular", " specific", " certain", " individual", " exact", " complete",
    " comprehensive", " considerable", " extensive", " first", " other", " one",
    " part", " person", " good", " perfect", " excellent", " right", " regular",
    " typical", " necessary", " proper", " specified", " limited", " whole", " standard",
}
SPECIFIER_VALUE = -1.0

DEGREE_OR_MIX = {
    " very", " pretty", " extremely", " really", " truly", " somewhat", " rather",
    " slightly", " completely", " entirely", " variety", " combination", " mix",
    " mixture", " bunch", " blend", " range", " different", " interesting", " exciting",
    " fun", " nice", " free", " difficult", " quick", " expected", " unexpected",
    " estimated", " helpful",
}
DEGREE_VALUE = 1.0

CJK_COPULAS = {
    "的是", "のは", "のも", "都是", "也是", "是一", "是非常", "とても", "かなり",
    "是一种", "是一個", "是一款", "のが", "するのは", "るのは",
}
CJK_VALUE = 1.0

TITLE_COLON_VALUE = 3.2


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return carry, 0.0
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    if word in CJK_COPULAS:
        return carry, CJK_VALUE
    if before == "Title" and word == ":":
        return carry, TITLE_COLON_VALUE
    if word == " one" and before in ONE_CONTEXTS:
        return carry, SPECIFIER_VALUE
    if before not in DETERMINERS:
        return carry, 0.0
    if word == " given":
        return carry, GIVEN_VALUE
    if word in SPECIFIERS:
        return carry, SPECIFIER_VALUE
    if word in DEGREE_OR_MIX:
        return carry, DEGREE_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

"""Phosphorus and sulfur word stems (negative activation).

The component goes strongly negative on the piece of a word that completes the stem of a
phosphorus or sulfur word: "phosph" (phosphate, phosphorylation, phosphatase), "sulf"
(sulfur, sulfate). It is weaker, about half, on the piece right after the stem while the
word is still unfinished ("or" in phosph|or, "at" in phosph|at|ase). Otherwise it is 0.
"""

READS = ()

STEMS = {"phosph": -9.0, "фосф": -9.0, "磷": -9.0, "sulf": -5.0, "сульф": -5.0, "硫": -5.0, "fluor": -3.0, "氟": -3.0}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # The current word: the newest token and the earlier pieces back to the word's start.
    pieces = []
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    for i in range(len(prefix.token_strings) - 1, -1, -1):
        if prefix.document_ids[i] != doc:
            break
        piece = prefix.token_strings[i].lower()
        letters = piece.lstrip(" ")
        if not letters.isalpha():
            break
        pieces.insert(0, letters)
        if piece[:1] == " ":
            break
    word = "".join(pieces)
    before = "".join(pieces[:-1])
    value = 0.0
    for stem, act in STEMS.items():
        if stem in word and stem not in before:
            value = min(value, act)  # this piece completes the stem
        elif pieces[:-1] and stem in before and stem not in before[: -len(pieces[-2])]:
            value = min(value, act / 2)  # the piece right after the completed stem
    return carry, value

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection, component 4420.

Plain-terms summary: a detector for the word "core" used as a piece of a compound
name (package, module or identifier), plus small side responses.

* Strong positive when the text ends in "core" attached after a separator or
  name: "-core" (jackson-core, 1.2), ".core" (org.springframework.core, 1.3),
  "_core" (0.8), "botocore" and "Glencore" (3), "/core" (packages/core, 0.5).
  Weaker for "core" after a space (" core", 0.15). Zero for "score" and "encore".
* Mild positive on runs of middle dots (leader lines), about 0.6.
* Negative on a short list of Chinese words for building, establishing and
  perfecting ("构建" construct, "完善" perfect, "健全" sound, "介" introduce,
  "泛" widespread), about -1.

Everywhere else it predicts 0. Most of the component's variance is small
everyday noise (std about 0.05 per token) that a short program does not model.

The carry holds the last few characters of the current document, so a word split
across tokens is still seen; it resets at each document start.
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

TAIL = 8
DOTS = 0.6
BUILD_ZH = {"构建", "構建", "构造", "构筑", "完善", "健全", "建立健全", "建", "構", "造", "介", "泛"}
BUILD_VALUE = -1.0


def core_value(before):
    if before in ("-", ".", "_"):
        return 1.2
    if before == "/":
        return 0.5
    if before == "s":
        return 0.0
    if before == " ":
        return 0.15
    if before.isalpha():
        return 0.3
    return 0.1


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    new_doc = len(prefix) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    tail = "" if new_doc or carry is None else carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = tail + token
    carry = text[-TAIL:]

    if text.lower().endswith("core"):
        return carry, core_value(text[-5:-4])
    if token and set(token) == {"·"}:
        return carry, DOTS
    if token in BUILD_ZH:
        return carry, BUILD_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4421, a rule-based predictor of its activation.

What it responds to, in plain terms:

1. Unfinished UTF-8 characters in polytonic Greek. Many Greek letters with breathing
   and accent marks are 3-byte characters whose middle byte the tokenizer emits alone.
   That token adds no visible character (its text decodes to U+FFFD), so the text does
   not change. When the surrounding text is Greek, this middle byte drives the
   component strongly negative (about -4.7 on average, -6 for the common E1 BC lead).
2. A doubled middle dot '··' (a dot leader), which the component also reads as about -1.2.
3. The colon in a 'Title:' that opens a new document right after <|endoftext|>. Here
   the component is at its maximum, about +6.8.

Everywhere else it predicts 0. Ablations show the Greek rule carries most of the score;
the other two rules add a little. The rule for other scripts (Hangul, CJK, Indic) was
left out: it changed the score by under 0.005.

Main program: go through the tokens in order, keeping the visible text decoded so far.
A token is "silent" if it is partial and the visible text is unchanged.
"""

READS = ()

GREEK = set(range(0x0370, 0x0400)) | set(range(0x1F00, 0x2000))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]:
        return carry, 0.0
    token = prefix.token_strings[t]
    if token == "··":
        return carry, -1.2
    if token == ":" and t >= 2 and prefix.token_strings[t - 1] == "Title":
        if prefix.token_strings[t - 2] == "<|endoftext|>":
            return carry, 6.8
    before = prefix.text_prefixes[t - 1]
    silent = "�" in token and prefix.text_prefixes[t] == before
    if silent and {ord(c) for c in before[-40:]} & GREEK:
        return carry, -4.7
    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4422 -- the archaic "here/there/where + particle" compound detector.

What it does
------------
This component goes strongly negative on the piece of a formal, legal-style compound
adverb that completes a "here-", "there-" or "where-" word, such as
  hereinafter, hereafter, hereunder, hereto, hereof  (about -8 to -12),
  thereto, thereunto, therefrom, thereof, therein, thereby, whereby  (about -2 to -8).
The activation sits on the completing token(s) (the "ina" and "fter" of "hereinafter",
the " thereof" token), and is near zero on the stem itself ("here", "there", "where")
and on ordinary words such as "therefore", "however", "whereas", "before".

The program keeps the current word in its carry (the letters since the last
space or punctuation mark, reset at each document start) and, while that word is a
here/there/where stem followed by a particle (after, of, to, unto, under, in, by, from, ...),
predicts a negative value: -6 for the "here" family and "unto" compounds, -3 for the
"there" and "where" family. Everything else is predicted as 0.

Why this shape
--------------
A word-identity table gives about 0.14-0.17 variance explained, and this rule gives about
0.21 on the same training scan with only one short list of stems and particles. The rest of
the variance is a long tail (German pronominal adverbs like "dadurch", "hierzu", "dorthin"; a few
"-ward" compass adverbs; "henceforth"; spurious positive pieces like "Thun") that a short
program does not cover. "therefore", "however" and "whereas" are excluded by the particle
list, since they are common and their activation is near zero.
"""

import re

READS = ()

STEMS = ("here", "there", "where", "hither", "whither", "whence")
PARTICLES = ("after", "inafter", "under", "unto", "upon", "to", "of", "from", "on",
             "by", "in", "into", "with", "within", "between", "through", "at", "abouts")
HERE_FAMILY = ("here",)
VALUE_HERE = -6.0
VALUE_THERE = -3.0


def _compound_value(word):
    """Negative value if `word` is a here/there/where compound (or a partial one), else 0."""
    for stem in STEMS:
        if word.startswith(stem) and len(word) > len(stem):
            rest = word[len(stem):]
            if any(p.startswith(rest) for p in PARTICLES):
                if stem in HERE_FAMILY or rest.startswith("unto"):
                    return VALUE_HERE
                return VALUE_THERE
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """carry: the current word so far (lowercase letters), or None at a row start."""
    word = carry or ""
    if len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        word = ""
    pieces = re.split(r"[^a-z]", prefix.token_strings[-1].lower())
    # letters after the last boundary character extend the word; a boundary starts a new one
    word = pieces[-1] if len(pieces) > 1 else word + pieces[0]
    return word, _compound_value(word)

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection component 4423.

What it does, in plain terms: it fires on the word "to" when "to" is a preposition
of extent or limit, as in "up to 6", "down to the present", "brought up to". It is
strongest right after "up" or "down" (about +7), moderate after "back" or "out"
("back to", "out to": about +2.7), weak after verbs of arriving or returning
("get to", "come to", "return to": about +1), and near zero for other uses,
including infinitive "to" ("need to", "able to"). The spelled-together "upto"
also fires (about +5). Everything else predicts 0.

The component also has large, sign-varying spikes on word-internal fragments of
Polish words (e.g. "rob|ek", "ior|stwa"). Their sign is not predictable from the
text seen so far, so this program leaves them at 0.

The program looks only at the current token and the one before it.
"""

READS = ()

UP_DOWN = ("up", "down")
BACK_OUT = ("back", "out")
ARRIVE_RETURN = ("get", "got", "come", "came", "comes", "return", "returned", "returning")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    if word == "upto":
        return carry, 5.0
    if word != "to" or len(prefix.token_strings) < 2:
        return carry, 0.0
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip()
    if before in UP_DOWN:
        return carry, 7.0
    if before in BACK_OUT:
        return carry, 2.7
    if before in ARRIVE_RETURN:
        return carry, 1.1
    return carry, 0.1

"""A negative response to addition and subtraction in expressions.

A short text buffer supplies arithmetic cues: digits, operators, powers,
and short variable names. These distinguish subtraction from prose hyphens.
Powers and numerical coefficients identify especially strong algebraic cases.
Spaced signs are generally stronger; programming punctuation weakens plus.
Other tokens get zero. Background and rare formatting responses are left
unexplained rather than memorizing token identities.
"""
import re

READS = ()
SIGN = re.compile(r'^[)\]}]*([+−-])(?![+−-])')
MONOMIAL = re.compile(
    r'(?:\^\{?\d+\}?|\b\d+[A-Za-z]+(?:\s+[A-Za-z])?)$'
)
LATEX = re.compile(r'\\(?:left|right|frac|sqrt|partial|sum|int)\b')


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    raw = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else b''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    state = (doc, (raw + prefix.token_bytes[-1])[-512:])
    match = SIGN.match(token.strip())
    if not match:
        return state, 0.0

    recent = raw.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')[-128:]
    left = recent.rstrip()
    word = re.search(r'\w+$', left)
    length = len(word[0]) if word else 0
    last = left[-1:]
    power = bool(last) and last in '⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹₀₁₂₃₄₅₆₇₈₉'
    close = bool(last) and last in ')]}'
    spaced = token[0].isspace()
    context = recent[-80:]
    operators = sum(ch in '=+*/^²³−' for ch in context)
    digits = sum(ch.isdecimal() for ch in context)
    code = sum(ch in ';[]{}_"' for ch in context)

    if power:
        value = -1.29
    elif MONOMIAL.search(left):
        value = -1.25 if spaced else -0.90
    elif LATEX.search(context) and (close or 1 <= length <= 2):
        value = -0.85 if spaced else -0.55
    elif match[1] != '+':
        if operators == 0:
            value = 0.0
        elif operators == 1:
            value = -0.20 if 1 <= length <= 2 else 0.0
        elif length == 1:
            value = -0.78 if spaced else -0.31
        elif close:
            value = -0.49
        elif spaced and length > 1:
            value = -0.43 if digits > 4 else -0.09
        else:
            value = 0.0
    elif digits:
        if operators > 5:
            value = -0.91 if code <= 2 else -0.58
        elif code <= 1:
            value = -0.71 if spaced else -0.39
        elif close:
            value = -0.54
        else:
            value = -0.28 if length else 0.0
    elif 1 <= length <= 3:
        value = -0.78 if spaced else -0.25
    elif length > 3:
        value = -0.10 if spaced else 0.0
    else:
        in_line = bool(recent.rsplit('\n', 1)[-1].strip())
        value = -0.31 if in_line and code <= 1 else 0.0
    return state, value
programs.haiku:
"""Plus and minus signs that join two terms of a formula.

Layer-1 MLP unit 4424 writes a strong negative signal at a binary '+' or '-'
that sits between two algebraic terms, e.g. the '+' in 'u² + v²', the '-' in
'x - 2', or the '+' in '(a + b)'. It is near zero on everything else: the
attached sign of a number ('-3'), a hyphen in a word ('well-known'), a sign
inside a number range, or a sign after '=' or '(' that opens an expression.

The program predicts a negative value there:
  * '+' weighs 1.0, a spaced '-' or '−' weighs 0.6, an unspaced '-' weighs 0.
  * The left-hand term sets the size: a single letter, digit or superscript
    gives 1.0, a closing bracket 0.7, a longer variable 0.7, and an English word
    0.2 (prose such as 'is - ' is not algebra).
  * The surrounding text sets the size: the more of the last 12 tokens look
    mathematical (digits, '=', '^', '*', '/', single letters, superscripts), the
    stronger the response, from 0.2 of the full size up to 1.0.
  * A run of repeated middle dots ('··', a degenerate filler line) gets its own
    fixed value of -0.66, except that a lone '··' in prose is ignored.
"""

READS = ()

SIGNS = {"+", "-", "−"}
SUPERSCRIPTS = set("²³¹⁰⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹₀₁₂₃₄₅₆₇₈₉")
BRACKETS = ")]}"


def term_size(prev):
    """How strongly the token before the sign is a term of a formula."""
    word = prev.strip()
    if not word:
        return 0.0
    last = word[-1]
    if len(word) == 1 and (word.isalnum() or last in SUPERSCRIPTS):
        return 1.0
    if last in SUPERSCRIPTS or last.isdigit():
        return 0.7
    if last in BRACKETS:
        return 0.7
    if last.isalpha():
        # a longer run of letters: a variable such as 'ab', or an English word
        is_prose_word = prev.startswith(" ") and len(word) >= 4
        return 0.2 if is_prose_word else 0.7
    return 0.0


def is_mathy(token):
    word = token.strip()
    if not word:
        return False
    return (
        any(ch.isdigit() for ch in word)
        or word in ("=", "^", "*", "/", "**")
        or (len(word) == 1 and word.isalpha())
        or word[-1] in SUPERSCRIPTS
    )


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    token = tokens[-1]
    if len(tokens) >= 2 and token == "··" and tokens[-2] == "··":
        return carry, -0.66
    if len(tokens) < 2 or token.strip() not in SIGNS:
        return carry, 0.0
    spaced = token.startswith(" ")
    if token.strip() == "+":
        weight = 1.0
    elif spaced:
        weight = 0.6
    else:
        return carry, 0.0
    size = term_size(tokens[-2])
    if size == 0.0:
        return carry, 0.0
    recent = tokens[max(0, len(tokens) - 13):-1]
    mathiness = sum(is_mathy(t) for t in recent) / 12
    context = 0.2 + 0.8 * min(1.0, 2 * mathiness)
    return carry, -weight * size * context

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4426, a document-start component.

It is almost silent inside a document. Its activity sits at the first token of a
document (where the model's attention can see nothing but that token): there it is
negative, about -0.4 on average. The strongest case is the digit '2' right after a
document-initial '1' (a document that opens with "12"), which drives it to about -5.4.
Everywhere else the program predicts 0.

Document starts are where the document id changes within a packed row, and positions
restart there, as the model does.
"""

READS = ()

START_VALUE = -0.4   # typical value at the first token of a document
TWELVE_VALUE = -5.4  # '2' right after a document-initial '1'


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]:
        return None, START_VALUE
    if t == 1 or docs[-2] != docs[-3]:
        if toks[-2] == "1" and toks[-1] == "2":
            return None, TWELVE_VALUE
    return None, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4427, in plain terms.

What it responds to:
1. Prepositions meaning "to" / "at" in other languages, written as separate words:
   French "à" and "au"/"aux", Spanish/Italian/Portuguese "a" and "al", Russian "на", "у",
   "от", Hungarian "á", Latin/Italian "ad". It fires strongly (about 0.6 to 1.0) on these.
   The English article "a" looks the same, so "a" (and "A", "am", "al", "ad", ...) only counts
   when the words just before it are not English but are common words of another language.
2. The first word of a document (the token after <|endoftext|>, or the first token of a row):
   a word there is pushed negative (about -0.3). Punctuation, spaces and digits there are near 0.
Everything else is predicted as 0. Only the current token and the few before it are read.
"""

READS = ()

# Preposition -> how strongly it fires when it is a separate word in foreign text.
TO_PREPOSITION = {
    "à": 1.0, "ad": 1.0, "á": 0.85, "у": 0.8, "a": 0.75, "aux": 0.65,
    "от": 0.6, "на": 0.6, "au": 0.55, "al": 0.3, "ao": 0.3, "am": 0.3,
}
# Common English words: if any appears in the window, a Latin-script "a" is the English article.
ENGLISH = set(
    "the of and is to in that with for on it as be are this from by at was an or which you your "
    "can".split()
)
# Common function words of French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese and similar languages.
FOREIGN = set(
    "de la el que en y los las del por para con una un es se le les des du et est qui pour dans "
    "il di che per da do um uma и в не на что с по как al lo o su sus si como más pero".split()
)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]  # the current token, with its leading space if it has one
    word = raw.strip()
    docs = prefix.document_ids

    # First token of a document (or of the row): a word there gives a negative value.
    if prefix.position == 0 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]:
        return None, (-0.3 if word[:1].isalpha() else 0.0)

    # Only a separate word (leading space) counts as a preposition.
    if not raw.startswith(" ") or word.lower() not in TO_PREPOSITION:
        return None, 0.0
    value = TO_PREPOSITION[word.lower()]

    # Latin-script forms are also English words ("a", "am", "al"), so check the language.
    if word.isascii():
        window = [w.strip().lower() for w in prefix.token_strings[-13:-1]]
        if any(w in ENGLISH for w in window) or sum(w in FOREIGN for w in window) < 1:
            return None, 0.0
    return None, value

"""Opening quotes of dictionary / JSON keys.

Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4428 fires on the quote mark that starts a key in an object
literal: the `"` or `'` after the comma that separates entries, e.g. the `"` before
`arguments` in `{"name": "bash", "arguments": ...}`, or the `'` before `Time` in
`{'Value': 1, 'Time': 2}`. Its strongest responses are inside the JSON tool calls the model
writes (`<tool_call>{"name": ...`). It stays silent on the value strings after `:`, and on
quotes in ordinary prose.

The program tracks which brackets are open (`{`, `[`, `(`) and resets at each document, so it
knows when the innermost bracket is an object. In that case, a key-opening quote scores 10 if
it is the first or second key after the comma, and 6 for later keys. A quote that opens the
first key right after a line break scores 4.5. An object-opening token (`{"`, `{'`) scores 2.7.
Everything else scores 0.
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    stack, keys, doc = carry if carry else ("", (), None)
    doc_now = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if doc_now != doc:
        stack, keys = "", ()
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].rstrip() if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    s = tok.lstrip()
    value = 0.0
    if s.startswith(('"', "'", '{"', "{'", '\\"')) and stack[-1:] == "{":
        if prev == "" or prev[-1] in ",{":
            n = keys[-1]
            if prev[-1:] == ",":
                value = 10.0 if n < 2 else 6.0
            else:
                value = 4.5
    if not value and s[:2] in ('{"', "{'"):
        value = 2.7
    keys = list(keys)
    for ch in tok:
        if ch in "{[(":
            stack += ch
            keys.append(0)
        elif ch in "})]" and stack:
            stack = stack[:-1]
            keys.pop()
    if value and keys and stack[-1:] == "{":
        keys[-1] += 1
    return (stack, tuple(keys), doc_now), value

"""Estimate a name- or specification-introducing noun phrase.

A decaying 'the' cue supplies a small baseline, raised for common English
label nouns and their WordNet noun inflections. Media labels also respond
to possessives and media-type modifiers. Geographical '[settlement] of'
constructions have a separate strong response on 'of'. State resets at
new documents; most initial tokens receive a small negative offset.
This is a broad-pattern approximation, not a complete lexical predictor.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()

# Different sorts of nouns that introduce a name, quotation, or specification.
GROUPS = (
    (2.12, 'word phrase term'),
    (1.01, 'name title expression sentence letter symbol character string'
           ' substring'),
    (2.82, 'genus phylum'),
    (1.41, 'equation inequality formula polynomial variable parameter'),
    (0.71, 'function integral matrix vector line plane point curve set group'
           ' number value digit integer pair ratio range interval sequence'),
    (1.02, 'album song band film movie show series poem book novel opera podcast'
           ' magazine journal newspaper website game play episode'),
    (0.88, 'year month period'),
    (0.77, 'file command macro tool'),
    (0.35, 'program method module class package directory'),
    (0.64, 'form style kind type species family entity'),
    (1.10, 'protein hormone enzyme gene molecule'),
)
WORDS = tuple(frozenset(words.split()) for _, words in GROUPS)
MEDIA = 5
POSSESSIVES = frozenset('his her its their our your my'.split())
MEDIA_MODIFIERS = frozenset('studio debut solo live rock pop jazz television '
                           'tv soundtrack titled untitled hit'.split())
GEOGRAPHY = (
    frozenset(('town', 'village')),
    frozenset(('city',)),
    frozenset('island country province region district kingdom republic field'.split()),
)
OF_SCORES = (3.66, 2.09, 0.84)
DECAY = 0.35


@lru_cache(maxsize=20000)
def label(token):
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if not word.isascii() or not word.isalpha():
        return -1, 1.0
    forms = set(wordnet.base_forms(word, 'noun')) | {word}
    for i, words in enumerate(WORDS):
        if forms & words:
            # Plural labels less often introduce one particular name.
            plural = word not in words
            return i, 0.65 if plural and i != 6 else 1.0
    return -1, 1.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    if first:
        previous, article, possessive = '', 0.0, 0.0
    else:
        _, previous, article, possessive = carry
    group, plurality = label(token)
    cue = article
    if group == MEDIA:
        cue = max(cue, possessive)
        if previous.lower() in MEDIA_MODIFIERS:
            cue = max(cue, 1.0)
    value = 0.07 * article
    if group >= 0 and token[:1].isspace():
        value = GROUPS[group][0] * plurality * cue
    if word == 'of':
        for names, score in zip(GEOGRAPHY, OF_SCORES):
            if previous.lower() in names:
                # A capitalized 'City' often belongs to the name itself.
                value = score * (0.25 if previous[:1].isupper() else 1.0)
                break
    if first:
        value = 0.0 if word == 'the' else -0.28
    article = 1.0 if word == 'the' else article * DECAY
    possessive = (1.0 if word in POSSESSIVES or word in ("'s", '’s')
                  else possessive * DECAY)
    if not word.isalpha():
        article = 0.0
        if word not in ("'s", '’s'):
            possessive = 0.0
    return (doc, token.strip(), article, possessive), float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4430: a "named kind" noun detector.

The component is quiet on almost every token. It fires on the word that sets up a specific
named thing: the head noun of a phrase that names a general kind, such as a label or name
(word, term, phrase, title), a creative work (album, film, band, book), a natural kind
(genus, enzyme, protein), or a mathematical or technical object (equation, formula,
function, value). It fires most strongly right after "the" ("the word", "the term",
"the genus", "the album"), because the next token is then usually a specific instance: a
quoted word, a title, a species name, a particular equation. Adjectives of fame before a
named item ("the famous", "the celebrated") fire too, and so does "of" after a settlement
noun ("the town of", "the city of"), since a place name comes next. Modifiers that make the
noun a named work or kind ("studio album", "television series") and possessives ("his
book") give a weaker response. Person titles ("the president") and everyday nouns
("the house") do not fire, and "a word" fires weakly.

The program is a few word lists with weights, set near the mean activations these words
have on training text:
  - label or natural-kind noun after "the":            1.25
  - creative-work, math or technical noun after "the": 0.95
  - adjective of fame after "the":                     1.4
  - "of" after a settlement noun:                      2.0 after "the", 0.9 otherwise
  - list noun after a work modifier:                   1.2
  - list noun after "his" or "her":                    0.6
  - the same nouns in any other context:               0.05
  - everything else:                                   0
"""

READS = ()

LABEL_OR_KIND = set("""word words term terms phrase keyword keywords name names title titles
heading headline label slogan designation symbol symbols letter letters trademark identifier
genus species enzyme protein antibody antigen drug molecule compound chemical bacteria
algae asteroid kinase hormone gene acid inhibitor disease""".split())

WORK_OR_TECHNICAL = set("""album albums film films movie book books song songs band series
show episode novel game games drama documentary play journal publication sitcom memoir magazine
equation equations inequality formula formulas function functions variable variables constant
identity integer integers decimal parameter polynomial theorem relation factor quantity
element condition curve attribute component group value values integral matrix sequence
ratio number numbers entity vector vectors interval limit set range point file files
directory instruction option entry line lines form expression expressions command string
statement notation""".split())

FAME_ADJECTIVES = set("famous celebrated iconic legendary renowned prestigious".split())

WORK_MODIFIERS = set("studio debut television tv compilation amino video animated drama music audio documentary".split())

POSSESSIVES = set("his her".split())

SETTLEMENTS = set("town city village island country district republic province region".split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    words = prefix.token_strings
    t = prefix.position
    cur = words[t].strip().lower()
    prev = ""
    before = ""
    if t > 0 and prefix.document_ids[t - 1] == prefix.document_ids[t]:
        prev = words[t - 1].strip().lower()
        if t > 1 and prefix.document_ids[t - 2] == prefix.document_ids[t]:
            before = words[t - 2].strip().lower()
    after_the = prev == "the"
    if cur == "of" and prev in SETTLEMENTS:
        return carry, 2.0 if before == "the" else 0.9
    if cur in FAME_ADJECTIVES:
        return carry, 1.4 if after_the else 0.0
    if not after_the:
        if cur in LABEL_OR_KIND or cur in WORK_OR_TECHNICAL:
            if prev in WORK_MODIFIERS:
                return carry, 1.2
            if prev in POSSESSIVES:
                return carry, 0.6
            return carry, 0.05
        return carry, 0.0
    if cur in LABEL_OR_KIND:
        return carry, 1.25
    if cur in WORK_OR_TECHNICAL:
        return carry, 0.95
    return carry, 0.0

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4431 (v1): a lexical detector for the Chinese/Korean
character 素 ("plain, element") and its near-kin characters (소, 索, 绿/綠, 紫, 裸), with
the frequent token '··' pulled slightly negative. Every other token predicts 0."""

READS = ()

# Activation (roughly) per token, from the training rows.
EXACT = {
    "素": 3.3,      # 素 itself: 素人, 酵素, 素早さ ...
    "소": 2.2,      # Korean 소 (so), also " 소"
    " 소": 1.5,
    "索": 1.5,      # 索 (suo), like 素 in form
    "绿": 3.0,      # green, simplified
    "綠": 3.5,      # green, traditional
    "绿色": 1.8,
    "紫": 1.1,      # purple
    "裸": -1.5,     # naked
    "··": -0.4,     # frequent filler token
}
# Words containing the character 素 or 绿/綠 get a weaker response.
CONTAINS = {"素": 1.0, "绿": 1.5, "綠": 1.5, "索": 0.8}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if tok in EXACT:
        return carry, float(EXACT[tok])
    best = 0.0
    for ch, v in CONTAINS.items():

    return carry, best

"""The quantifier "all" detector (layers.1.mlp.down_proj, component 4432).

This component writes a strong negative signal when the word being read is "all" or a
translation of it, and is near zero on everything else. How strong depends on the word:

  French / Italian  tout, toute, toutes, tous, tutto, tutta, tutti, tutte, and Italian
                    compounds ending -tutto/-tutti/-tutta/-tutte, and "partout":     about -9
  Spanish / Portuguese  todo, toda, todos, todas, tudo, totes, tots:                about -7
  first pieces of those words, when the word is split (e.g. "tut" before "ta"):     about -3
  other languages   tot, toate, toàn, toți, toată, alle, все, всех, ...:            about -2
  English "all":    about -0.9 (in "at all" and "after all" it is ~0).

Words are read from the text: a word is the letters of the newest token plus any earlier
tokens that continue it, so a word split across tokens fires on the piece that completes
it. Capitalised forms ("Tout", "All") count; all-caps or mixed-case code tokens ("TODO",
"ToDo") do not. Other quantifiers ("every", "each", "whole", "any", "both") stay at 0.
What it does not capture: the diffuse small activations everywhere else, which are noise
around zero.
"""
import re

READS = ()

FRENCH_ITALIAN = {"tout", "toute", "toutes", "tous", "tutto", "tutta", "tutti", "tutte"}
IBERIAN = {"todo", "toda", "todos", "todas", "tudo", "totes", "tots"}
OTHER_LANGUAGES = {"tot", "toate", "toàn", "toți", "toată", "alle", "alles", "все", "всё",
                   "всех", "всей", "всего", "весь", "вся"}
PARTIAL = {w[:k] for w in FRENCH_ITALIAN | IBERIAN for k in range(3, len(w))}
IDIOM_BEFORE = {"at", "after"}
TAIL_LETTERS = re.compile(r"[^\W\d_]*$")


def current_word(token_strings):
    """Letters of the newest token and of the earlier tokens that continue its word."""
    word = ""
    for piece_text in reversed(token_strings):
        piece = TAIL_LETTERS.search(piece_text).group(0)
        word = piece + word
        if piece != piece_text:  # this token has a space or punctuation before the piece
            break
    return word


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    strings = prefix.token_strings
    word = current_word(strings)
    lower = word.lower()
    cased_ok = word == lower or (word[:1].isupper() and word[1:].islower())
    if not cased_ok:
        return None, 0.0
    if lower in FRENCH_ITALIAN or lower.endswith(("tutto", "tutti", "tutta", "tutte", "partout")):
        return None, -9.0
    if lower in IBERIAN:
        return None, -7.0
    if lower in PARTIAL:
        return None, -3.0
    if lower in OTHER_LANGUAGES:
        return None, -2.0
    if lower == "all":
        before = strings[-2].strip().lower() if len(strings) > 1 else ""
        return None, 0.0 if before in IDIOM_BEFORE else -0.9
    return None, 0.0

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4433 -- the "ti / ia" word-piece detector.

What it does, in plain terms: the component is silent on most text and wakes up on short
pieces of longer words that contain the letters "ti" or "i", the way Latin- and
Romance-style words are spelled (initiate, anti-, -ation, -ati-, -iti-, -ți). It is
strongest on the piece "ti" and its close relatives ("ati", "iti", "ti", "ți", "enti",
"stit", "uti") when they close off a word that was split into pieces; medium on the
roots "anti" and "initiat-"; weak on other short pieces containing "i" ("ia", "ii", "ie",
"i"). Whole words, punctuation, digits, spaces and the rest of the vocabulary predict 0.

The program only looks at the current token, so it is stateless: `step` returns the
expected activation for the newest token and ignores the rest of the prefix.
"""

READS = ()

# Pieces that spell the "ti" sound of Latin-style words: strongest response.
TI_PIECES = {"ati", "iti", "ti", "ți", "enti", "stit", "Ti", "uti"}
# Word roots that contain "ti": medium response.
TI_ROOTS = ("anti", "initiat", "initi")
# Short vowel-i pieces: weak response.
I_PIECES = {"ia", "ii", "ie", "i"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # The newest token, without its leading space (" anti" is the piece "anti").
    piece = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    if piece in TI_PIECES:
        return None, 1.0
    if piece.lower().startswith(TI_ROOTS) or piece.lower() == "anti":
        return None, 0.6
    if piece in I_PIECES:
        return None, 0.1
    if piece.isalpha() and len(piece) <= 3 and "i" in piece:
        return None, 0.02
    return None, 0.0

"""Opening brackets that start an aside in prose (layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4435).

The component fires on an opening bracket, mostly a space-led " (", that opens a
parenthetical, gloss or abbreviation in running text, e.g. "Xiaohong (Xiaohong)" or
"the Hungarian Working People's Party (abbr.)". It stays quiet on "(" that follows a
control keyword in code ("if (", "for (", "switch ("). The first token of each row
gets a small negative value.

Main idea: predict 1.5 at " (" or "（", 0.9 at other opening brackets with no letters
or digits, and 0 elsewhere. Brackets right after if/for/while/switch/elif/foreach are 0.
"""
import re

READS = ()

CONTROL = {"if", "for", "while", "switch", "elif", "foreach"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0:
        return None, -0.5
    tok = prefix.token_strings[t]
    if not any(c in tok for c in "([（【") or re.search(r"\w", tok):
        return None, 0.0
    prev = prefix.token_strings[t - 1].strip()
    if prev in CONTROL:
        return None, 0.0
    return None, 1.5 if tok in (" (", "（") else 0.9

"""Sparse responses to typography, UTF-8 fragments, and damaged encodings.

Most ordinary tokens get zero. Fractions and superscripts usually get positive
values; hex escapes, selected Indic prefixes, and Arabic/Hebrew marks get
negative ones. Recent text adjusts for mojibake, number-form fragments near
Han characters, and pure middle-dot filler. A small separate rule handles the
blank line after </think>. All state resets at document boundaries.
These are empirical approximations, not a general Unicode decoder.
"""
import unicodedata
import regex

READS = ()

# Unicode's names make these Arabic pronunciation marks explicit.
ARABIC_MARKS = {
    'FATHA': -4.3,
    'SHADDA': -3.78,
    'DAMMA': -1.2,
    'KASRA': -1.62,
    'SUKUN': -1.13,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    fresh = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    tail = '' if fresh else carry[1]
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    only_dots = (fresh or carry[2]) and bool(text) and not text.strip('·')
    raw = prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    s = text.strip()
    b = raw.strip()
    last_char = tail[-1:]
    digit_before = last_char.isdigit()
    value = 0.0

    # A character split between tokens can have a response on both pieces.
    previous_raw = (prefix.token_bytes[-2] if prefix.position > 0
                    and prefix.document_ids[-2] == doc else b'')
    completed = (previous_raw + raw).decode('utf8', 'ignore')[-1:]
    number_form = previous_raw == b'\xe2\x85'
    fraction = (completed and unicodedata.name(completed, '')
                .startswith('VULGAR FRACTION'))
    if number_form and fraction:
        value = 12.2 if unicodedata.numeric(completed) == 3 / 8 else 8.5
    elif (previous_raw == b'\xd6' and completed
          and unicodedata.category(completed) == 'Mn'):
        value = -2.4
    elif raw in (b'\xe0\xa8', b'\xe0\xa9', b'\xe0\xb0', b'\xe0\xb1'):
        # Unspaced, unfinished Indic letters; upper halves contain vowel signs.
        gurmukhi = b[1] in (0xa8, 0xa9)

                            range(max(0, prefix.position - 2), prefix.position)
                            if prefix.document_ids[i] == doc)
        previous = previous.decode('utf8', 'ignore')[-1:]
        mark = previous and unicodedata.category(previous).startswith('M')
        factor = 1.0 if previous.isalpha() else 0.85 if mark else 0.3
        value = (-11.8 if gurmukhi else -8.0) * factor
        if b[1] & 1:
            value *= 0.38 if gurmukhi else 0.31
    elif raw == b'\xe0\xae':  # Unfinished Tamil letter.
        value = -3.0

What it does, in plain terms: it fires on the lone space token that opens an indented
line. A two-space indent is tokenised as a bare space followed by a space-led word, so
the bare space is the token to watch. It fires about 0.8 when that space follows a real
newline, and about 1.3 when it follows an escaped newline (a backslash and n, as in code
or text embedded in a JSON or string literal). It also fires about 0.8 on a doubled
backslash token (typically an escaped newline inside escaped code; LaTeX line breaks
(\\) do the opposite, around -1), about 1.9 on runs of middle dots (dotted leaders),
and very strongly (about 10) on the colon of a document-initial 'Title:' header, the one
rare, very large spike seen. Everything else predicts 0.

BS = chr(92)

    s = prefix.token_strings
    cur = s[-1]
    prev = s[-2] if len(s) > 1 else ""
    prev2 = s[-3] if len(s) > 2 else ""

            return None, 0.8
        if prev == "n" and prev2.endswith(BS) or prev == BS + "n":
            return None, 1.3

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 4449: a document-opening detector.

What it does: the component is silent in the middle of a document. Only the first
token of each document (the first token of a row, or the first token after a new
document id) gets a value, and that value depends only on which token it is: the
attention at that position sees nothing but itself, so the token's own identity sets
the response. Opening tokens that look like a title or label word ("Video", "Color",
"Seattle", a CJK noun) push the component positive; opening tokens that are code or
markup syntax ("(\\"", "::", " &", "://"), closed-class function words ("the", "of",
"and"), and lowercase word fragments with no leading space push it negative.

The value is a short linear score over those word-shape classes, not a lookup of
token ids, so it captures the sign and rough size of the response but not the
token-by-token detail. A full per-token table would explain far more of the variance
(see the explanation), at the cost of being unreadable.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Closed-class English words; a document that opens with one is usually mid-sentence.
FUNCTION_WORDS = frozenset(
    "a an the of and or but to in on at by for with from as is are was were be been "
    "it its this that these those i you he she we they me my your his our their not no "
    "so if than when which who what how there do does have has had will would can should".split()
)

TITLE_WORD = re.compile(r"\s*[A-Z][a-z]+")  # "Video", " Color"
CAPITALISED = re.compile(r"\s*[A-Z]")  # any capital initial
LOWER_WORD = re.compile(r"\s*[a-z]+")  # "the", " of"
CODE_SYMBOL = re.compile(r"[()\[\]{}=:\\/&^;<>|`#$+*]")  # code and markup syntax
CJK = re.compile(r"[぀-鿿가-힯]")  # Chinese, Japanese, Korean
PURE_PUNCT = re.compile(r"[^\w\s]+")


def opening_value(token):
    """Linear score for a token that opens a document, from its word shape."""
    text = token.strip()
    title = bool(TITLE_WORD.fullmatch(token))
    lower = bool(LOWER_WORD.fullmatch(token))
    score = -0.31  # baseline
    score += 0.72 * title
    score += -0.17 * (bool(CAPITALISED.match(token)) and not title)
    score += 0.27 * (lower and token.startswith(" "))  # " word" after a space
    score += -0.44 * (lower and not token.startswith(" "))  # word fragment
    score += -0.82 * (text.lower() in FUNCTION_WORDS)
    score += -0.54 * bool(CODE_SYMBOL.search(token))
    score += 0.74 * bool(CJK.search(token))
    score += 0.33 * (text == "")  # whitespace only
    score += -0.26 * (bool(PURE_PUNCT.fullmatch(token)) and text != "")
    score += 0.84 * min(len(text), 12) / 12  # longer words sit higher
    return score

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    opens_document = (
        prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    )
    if not opens_document:
        return carry, 0.0
    return carry, float(opening_value(token))

What it does, in plain terms
    This component writes into the residual stream only when a line in the first
    few lines of a document begins with indentation: a token made purely of spaces
    and/or tabs, right after a newline. For such a token it pushes the activation
    strongly negative, and the push fades quickly as the document goes on:

        line 2 of the document (one newline before)   about -0.6
        line 3                                        about -0.15
        line 4                                        about -0.09
        ...                                           about 0 by line 8 or so

    The fade is close to -0.6 / (line number)**2, where the line number counts
    the newlines seen so far in the document (line 1 is the first line).
    Everywhere else the component is near zero: its typical activation is
    a diffuse +-0.03 noise that no simple rule captures.

    Why: the model's first few lines of a document have little context, and an
    indented first line (a code block, a list item, a quoted passage) is a strong
    cue about the kind of text that follows. This component is a small,
    early-position indentation detector, not a general whitespace feature: the
    same indentation deep inside a document is essentially silent.

Scope / limits
    * Predicts 0 for every other token, including the first token of a document
      (its activation depends on the token itself, with no simple class pattern).
    * Captures the largest, most readable part of the variance; the remaining
      variance is diffuse noise.

READS is empty: the program needs only the token strings and document ids.
"""

READS = ()

INDENT_CHARS = " \t"


def _is_indent(token: str) -> bool:
    """True for a non-empty run of spaces and tabs only (no newline, no text)."""
    return token != "" and all(c in INDENT_CHARS for c in token)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]

    # document, whether the previous token ended a line)
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:

        lines_before, prev_newline = 0, False

    if prev_newline and _is_indent(token):

        value = -0.6 / lines_before**2

    return (doc, lines_before + int(ends_line), ends_line), value

"""Separator-line detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4451.

This component is mostly silent. It goes strongly negative on the tokens that make up
long visual rules: a token that is one run of the same ruler character (=, -, _, #, /, *, ~)
repeated many times, such as "================" or "////////". The longer the rule, the more
negative. It also goes moderately negative on the Java annotation "@Override" (and the bare
"Override" that follows "@"). Everywhere else it sits near zero.

The program predicts the activation from the token's text alone:
  - a ruler run of 64+ characters   -> -6.5
  - a ruler run of 32 to 63         -> -3
  - a ruler run of 8 to 31          -> -0.5
  - "@Override" / "Override"        -> -4.2 / -3
  - anything else                   -> 0
"""

RULER_CHARS = set("=-_#/*~")
OVERRIDE = {"@Override": -4.2, "Override": -3.0}


def ruler_length(text):
    """Length of the longest run of one repeated ruler character in the token's text."""
    best, run, prev = 0, 0, ""
    for ch in text:
        run = run + 1 if ch == prev else 1
        prev = ch
        if ch in RULER_CHARS and run > best:
            best = run
    return best

    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if text.strip() in OVERRIDE:
        return carry, OVERRIDE[text.strip()]
    n = ruler_length(text)
    if n >= 64:

    if n >= 32:
        return carry, -3.0
    if n >= 8:
        return carry, -0.5
    return carry, 0.0

MLIKE = "mмμ"

expression, especially a dictionary-labelled
idiom: either its third character, or its whole final two-character token.

LARGE_COUNTS = set("百千萬万")
PAIR_MARKERS = NEGATORS | set("一二三四五六七八九十百千万萬兩两")

GRAMMATICAL_WORDS = set(
    "的地得了着著过過吗嗎呢啊吧呀哦嘛啦"
    "我你您他她它们們这這那谁誰"
    "和与與及于於是有在也都很就"
)

_meanings, _spellings = cedict._table()
WORDS = set()
IDIOMS = set()
for _word, _entries in _spellings.items():
    if len(_word) == 4 and HAN.fullmatch(_word):
        WORDS.add(_word)
        if any("idiom" in _meanings[i] for i in _entries):
            IDIOMS.add(_word)
WORD_PREFIXES = {w[:3] for w in WORDS}
IDIOM_PREFIXES = {w[:3] for w in IDIOMS}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    previous = "" if first else carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    carry = (doc, (previous + token)[-2:])

        if token == "//\n":

        elif token == "<!":

        elif token in {"import", "package"}:

            if token in GRAMMATICAL_WORDS:

            if token in NEGATORS:
                value = -0.52
            if token in SMALL_COUNTS:
                value = -0.55
            if token in LARGE_COUNTS:
                value = -0.85
            fragment = previous + token
            if fragment in IDIOM_PREFIXES:
                value -= 1.85
            elif fragment in WORD_PREFIXES:
                value -= 0.55
            if len(previous) == 2 and HAN.fullmatch(previous):

            fragment = previous + token

"""Approximate the negative signal on noun-complement prepositions.

Action nouns and nominal endings suggest a noun taking a complement, rather
than a verb followed by a preposition. A preceding determiner strengthens this
reading. 'Of' is usually weaker. Dictionary classes, word length and frequency
are coarse cues: this does not memorize individual noun/preposition pairs.
Other tokens stay near zero; the short text buffer resets at each document.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
ENGLISH = frozenset("""
of to for in on from with at by about into over between through without
under after before against upon that
""".split())
FOREIGN = frozenset("""
de des du del di da en para por entre con von für mit an auf zu zur aus bei
""".split())
DETERMINERS = frozenset("""
a an the this that these those my his her its our their
""".split())
NOMINAL_ENDINGS = (
    "tion", "sion", "ment", "ness", "ity", "ance", "ence", "ship"
)


@lru_cache(maxsize=8192)
def dictionary(word):
    return (wordnet.parts_of_speech(word), wordnet.categories(word, "noun"),
            zipf_frequency(word.lower(), "en"))


def estimate(prep, tail):
    match = re.search(r"([^\W\d_]+)$", tail)
    previous = match.group(1) if match else ""
    before = tail[:match.start()] if match else ""
    words = re.findall(r"[^\W\d_]+", before.lower())
    determiner = bool(words and words[-1] in DETERMINERS)
    pos, categories, frequency = dictionary(previous)
    word = previous.lower()

    # Action nouns: a determiner helps separate noun and verb uses.
    if "noun.act" in categories:
        if prep == "of":
            return -0.135
        if len(word) <= 5:
            return -0.818 if determiner else -0.253
        if word.endswith("ing"):
            return -0.172
        if prep == "that":
            return -0.232
        return -1.622 if determiner else -0.993

    # Productive endings provide a cue even outside the dictionary.
    if word.endswith(NOMINAL_ENDINGS):
        return -0.166 if prep == "of" else -1.0
    if "noun" not in pos:
        return -0.151 if prep in FOREIGN else 0.006
    if prep == "for":
        return -0.643
    if prep == "of":
        return -0.02
    if frequency > 5.5:
        return -0.027
    return -1.112 if prep == "about" else -0.24

    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    tail = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == document else ""
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prep = token.strip().lower()
    value = 0.0038
    boundary = token[:1].isspace() or not tail or tail[-1:].isspace()
    if boundary and (prep in ENGLISH or prep in FOREIGN):
        value = estimate(prep, tail)
    return (document, (tail + token)[-100:]), value

not try to. The doc-start values are token-specific in sign within each class, so the class

"""Recognize chi/chin fragments and weaker hi/shi fragments.

Also recognize i beginning a token immediately after h, especially ch.
Longer i-pieces fade; ing and icht weaken this response. Case, a preceding
path separator, and document starts adjust its strength. Accents and
Greek/Cyrillic transliterations are discounted. This is a local spelling
approximation, not a vocabulary lookup or a semantic China detector.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import unicodedata
import regex
from anyascii import anyascii

READS = ()

# Split h+i: columns are i alone, i+vowel, i+nasal, i+s, i+other.
SPLIT = {
    'ch': (6.7, 1.8, 2.7, 4.1, 1.3),
    'sh': (3.1, 0.4, 0.4, 0.9, 0.0),
    'ph': (2.6, 0.1, 0.4, 0.7, 0.0),
    'th': (1.6, 0.15, 0.17, 0.17, 0.0),
    'h':  (2.2, 0.1, 0.1, 0.75, -0.3),
}


@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def spelling(text):
    scale = 1.0
    if regex.search(r'[\p{Greek}\p{Cyrillic}]', text):
        text, scale = anyascii(text), 0.6
    folded = unicodedata.normalize('NFD', text)
    if any(unicodedata.combining(c) for c in folded):
        scale *= 0.7
    return ''.join(c for c in folded
                   if not unicodedata.combining(c)).lower(), scale


def activation(token, previous, first):
    q, scale = spelling(token.strip())
    old, old_scale = spelling(previous)
    response = 0.0
    if q == 'chi':
        response = 3.0 + 3.0 * token.strip()[0].isupper()
        response += 3.0 * first + 4.5 * previous.endswith('/')
    elif q == 'chin':
        response = 5.3
    elif q.startswith('chin'):
        response = 2.6 * 0.5 ** (len(q) - 5)
    elif q == 'chic':
        response = 1.9
    elif q.startswith('chic'):
        response = 0.5 / (len(q) - 3)
    elif q.endswith('chi'):
        response = 1.8
    elif q.endswith('shi'):
        response = 1.0
    elif q.endswith('hi'):
        response = 0.42
    value = -0.001 - 0.28 * first + scale * response
    if token.strip() == 'チ':
        value += 0.9  # Katakana chi.
    if not first and token and not token[0].isspace() and old.endswith('h'):
        # Wade-Giles sometimes writes the split as ch + 'i.
        piece = q.lstrip("'")
        if piece.startswith('i'):
            cluster = old[-2:] if old[-2:] in SPLIT else 'h'
            second = piece[1:2]
            column = (0 if not second else 1 if second in 'aeiou' else
                      2 if second in 'mn' else 3 if second == 's' else 4)
            split = SPLIT[cluster][column] * 0.65 ** max(0, len(piece) - 2)
            if cluster == 'ch':
                split -= 1.5 * piece.startswith('ing')
                split -= 1.3 * piece.startswith('icht')
                split += 3.3 * (len(old) > 2 and old[-3] in '/.-_')
                split += 4.0 * (piece == 'i' and token.isupper()
                                and previous.endswith('CH'))
            value += min(scale, old_scale) * split
    return float(value)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != document
    previous = '' if first else carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    return (document, token), activation(token, previous, first)

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection component 4466: a "chi / China" spelling detector.

What it does: the component is silent almost everywhere. It switches on when the
text being written has just completed the syllable "chi" (or "chin"/"china"):
the token "Chi" in names (Chihiro, Chicago, Chinook), "China" and "Chin-", and the
split pieces "ch" + "i", "ch" + "in" or "Coch" + "in". It is strongest for the
capitalised "Chi" and weaker for lower-case "chi". It responds a little to
"shi"/"ghi" and to "Chinese". At the first token of each document it is slightly
negative. Everything else is treated as zero.

The program only reads the running text of the current document, which is reset at
each document boundary (the model's attention is reset there too).
"""

READS = ()

DOC_START = -0.28    # first token of a document
CHI_CAPITAL = 6.5    # the text now ends in "Chi"
CHI_LOWER = 3.5      # the text now ends in "chi"
CHIN = 5.5           # the text now ends in "chin"
CHINA_CAPITAL = 2.8  # the text now ends in "China"
CHINA_LOWER = 3.6    # the text now ends in "china"
CHINESE = 1.0        # the text now ends in "Chinese"
SHI_GHI = 1.5        # the text now ends in "shi" or "ghi"

KEEP = 12            # characters of running text kept in the carry


def activation(text):
    """Prediction for a token that leaves `text` (this document so far) ending as it does."""
    low = text.lower()
    if low.endswith("chi"):
        return CHI_CAPITAL if text.endswith("Chi") else CHI_LOWER
    if low.endswith("chin"):
        return CHIN
    if low.endswith("china"):
        return CHINA_CAPITAL if text.endswith("China") else CHINA_LOWER
    if low.endswith("chinese"):
        return CHINESE
    if low.endswith("shi") or low.endswith("ghi"):
        return SHI_GHI
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """One position: extend the running text of this document by the newest token."""
    new_document = (
        len(prefix) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    )
    if new_document:
        return prefix.token_strings[-1][-KEEP:], DOC_START
    text = ((carry or "") + prefix.token_strings[-1])[-KEEP:]
    return text, activation(text)

"""Negative on the "sh" sound [sh] spelled inside words.

The component's activation is near zero on ordinary text and goes negative on
the pieces of a word that carry an "sh" sound: sh, Sh, SH, sz (Polish), and the
š, ş, ś, ш, ش letters of Czech, Turkish, Polish, Cyrillic and Arabic.

Its size depends on how the sound is spelled out:
- a split sound, where the "h" completes "sh" across two tokens ("S" + "h",
  "s" + "hip"), is strongest;
- a short standalone piece with the sound ("sh", "Sh", "-sh", "ш") is fairly strong;
- a longer token that happens to contain "sh" ("shown", "shares", "English",
  "she", "should") is weak;
- further pieces of a word whose sh-sound already appeared are moderate.

The program tracks the current word (the letters since the last non-letter
token, reset at each document start) and labels each token with one of these
cases. Each case value is the mean activation for that case on training text.
It does not model the rare non-sh negatives (a long tail of word fragments and
other scripts), which is why it explains about a sixth of the variance.
"""

READS = ()

SH_SPELLINGS = ("sh", "sz", "š", "ş", "ś", "ш", "ش")

SPLIT_COMPLETED = -2.4   # the sound is completed here, the token has no sh itself ("h" in "S|h")
STANDALONE_PIECE = -0.7  # a short token containing the sound ("sh", "Sh", "ш")
WHOLE_WORD = -0.3        # a longer token containing the sound ("shown", "English")
CONTINUED_PIECE = -0.8   # a short piece of a word whose sound already appeared
CONTINUED_LONGER = -0.5  # a longer piece after the sound already appeared


def has_sh(text):
    return any(spelling in text for spelling in SH_SPELLINGS)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].lower()
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev_word, prev_doc = carry if carry is not None else ("", None)
    if doc != prev_doc or not token[:1].isalpha():
        prev_word = ""
    word = prev_word + token.lstrip()
    short = len(token.strip()) <= 3
    if has_sh(prev_word):
        value = CONTINUED_PIECE if short else CONTINUED_LONGER
    elif has_sh(word) and has_sh(token):
        value = STANDALONE_PIECE if short else WHOLE_WORD
    elif has_sh(word):
        value = SPLIT_COMPLETED
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return (word, doc), value

The unit fires on double-newline tokens (a blank line: "\\n\\n", "\\r\\n\\r\\n", ".\\n\\n", "}\\n\\n", ...).
Its strength depends on the character just before the break:
  - a bare break, or one after a closing bracket, quote, semicolon or backtick: strong
  - after sentence-final punctuation (. ? !): weak
  - after a colon: weaker; after a comma or a space: about zero

structural, and slightly stronger when the recent text has many line breaks.
Everything else predicts 0. Only the strength of the break is modelled; the unit's
small diffuse activity on ordinary tokens is not.
"""

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    seen_chat, doc = carry if carry is not None else (False, None)
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != doc:  # a new document: forget the chat context
        seen_chat, doc = False, prefix.document_ids[-1]
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if any(m in s for m in CHAT_MARKERS):
        seen_chat = True
    carry = (seen_chat, doc)
    if s.count("\n") < 2 and s.count("\r") < 2:
        return carry, 0.0
    body = s.rstrip("\r\n")
    if body == "":
        base = 0.8
    elif body == " ":
        base = 0.08
    elif body[-1] in ".?!":
        base = 0.25
    elif body[-1] == ":":
        base = 0.15
    elif body[-1] == ",":

    else:

    breaks = sum(("\n" in x) for x in recent)
    value = base + 0.02 * breaks + (0.25 if seen_chat else 0.0)
    return carry, value

    value += 0.204 * (word=='following')

each document (where a row starts, or where the packed document changes): there it dips.
The dip is deeper when the document opens on a lowercase word (a text starting mid-sentence,

LOWERCASE_START_VALUE = -0.38
OTHER_START_VALUE = -0.15


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    starts_document = t == 0 or ids[t] != ids[t - 1]

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4478 -- a "qu / gu" spelling detector.

What it does: it fires on the letter u of a q-u or g-u spelling (the /k/ or /g/ sound
before a vowel: qu, gu, que, ue, ...) when that spelling sits inside a short word piece
of a word that is still being spelled out. Whole English words such as "question",
"arguments" or "request" do not fire, and neither do long pieces.

Three cases, with strengths measured on training text:
  1. The piece itself contains qu/gu and is 2-4 letters: "gu" (Bou|gu), "que", "qu",
     "ique". Shorter pieces are stronger.
  2. A piece starting u, ue or ui right after a piece that ends in q or g:
     "Deng|ue", "Leg|u", "Marg|uer", "Ag|uil". These are the strongest.
  3. Anything else is 0.

The word is rebuilt from the tokens back to the last space or non-letter, in the same
document, so the rule uses only the text so far.
"""

import re

READS = ()
MAX_PIECE = 4  # longer pieces are whole words or word endings: no response


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    strings, docs = prefix.token_strings, prefix.document_ids
    t = len(strings) - 1
    # The word so far: the current token and earlier tokens of the same word.
    word = ""
    for i in range(t, -1, -1):
        if docs[i] != docs[t]:
            break
        s = strings[i]
        word = s.lstrip(" ") + word
        if s.startswith(" ") or not s.lstrip(" ").isalpha():
            break
    piece = strings[t].lstrip(" ")
    # Only a letter-only piece that does not start a new word (no leading space).
    if strings[t].startswith(" ") or not piece.isalpha() or len(piece) > MAX_PIECE:
        return None, 0.0
    if not re.search("[qg]u", word.lower()):
        return None, 0.0
    n = len(piece)
    low = piece.lower()
    # Case 1: the qu/gu digraph is inside this piece.
    if re.search("[qg]u", low):
        return None, {2: 3.0, 3: 1.6}.get(n, 1.1)
    # Case 2: a u-piece right after a piece ending in q or g.
    if re.match("u($|[aei])", low) and docs[t - 1] == docs[t] and strings[t - 1][-1:].lower() in ("q", "g"):
        return None, 4.0
    # Case 3: the qu/gu is earlier in this word; a weak response on short pieces.
    return None, 0.6 if n <= 3 else 0.2

"""Markdown / number-sign "#" detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4479.

The component goes negative on a bare run of hash signs ("#", " #", "##", ...),
as a markdown heading, a hashtag or a "#" in prose does. A single "#" is about
-1.2 and "##" about -1.5 (and about -1.7 when it starts a line); "###" and longer
runs are weaker, about -0.7. The first token of a document is positive, about
+0.9. Every other token gives 0: the component is nearly silent elsewhere.

Caveat: the size varies a lot between "#" tokens (std about 1.3). The simple
context features tried (code vs prose, line start, indentation, earlier headings)
explain little of that spread.

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    run = token.strip()
